- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with momentum.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive sell-off.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 7-day average is trending upward.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misaligns with sentiment shift — adjust forecast to match sentiment direction 2–3 days ahead.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward sentiment, model often fails to capture continuation — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias.  
- If true outcome exceeds model by >2% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overfitting to recent spikes.
